controls.name: Processes and mechanisms for managing all components of network security controls (NSCs) are documented, kept current, and operational.
controls.description: Evidence: Network security policy; NSC configuration standards; version history; review sign-offs

controls.name: Roles and responsibilities for performing activities under Requirement 1 are documented, assigned, and understood.
controls.description: Evidence: RACI or responsibility matrix; job descriptions; signed acknowledgment records

controls.name: Configuration standards for NSCs address all applicable security risks.
controls.description: Evidence: NSC configuration standards; approved rule-set templates; risk justification records

controls.name: All permitted services, protocols, and ports are identified, approved, and have a defined business justification.
controls.description: Evidence: Approved services/ports/protocols list; firewall rule justification log; change management tickets

controls.name: An accurate network diagram showing all CDE connections to other networks is maintained and current.
controls.description: Evidence: Network diagram(s) with date; CDE boundary clearly marked; connection inventory

controls.name: An accurate data-flow diagram showing all account data flows across systems and networks is maintained.
controls.description: Evidence: Data-flow diagram with CHD/SAD flows shown; review dates and approvals

controls.name: All services, protocols, and ports in use are reviewed at least every six months.
controls.description: Evidence: Bi-annual review records; updated approved services list; reviewer sign-offs

controls.name: Security features are defined and implemented for all insecure services, protocols, or ports in use.
controls.description: Evidence: Insecure protocol register; compensating controls documentation; TLS/SSH version configs

controls.name: NSC configurations are reviewed at least every six months to confirm they are relevant and effective.
controls.description: Evidence: Bi-annual config review logs; review checklist; approver sign-offs

controls.name: NSC configuration files are protected from unauthorized access and kept consistent with active network configurations.
controls.description: Evidence: Access controls on config files; FIM alerts; change management records comparing backup to live

controls.name: Network and data-flow diagrams are kept current, reviewed at least every 12 months or on significant change.
controls.description: Evidence: 12-month or on-change review evidence; version history; change-triggered update records

controls.name: All connections between the CDE and third-party/cloud environments are documented and reviewed.
controls.description: Evidence: Third-party connection register; cloud connectivity documentation; approved connection records

controls.name: Inbound traffic to the CDE is restricted to only traffic that is necessary.
controls.description: Evidence: Firewall inbound rule-set; deny-all default rule evidence; approved inbound service list

controls.name: Outbound traffic from the CDE is restricted to only traffic that is necessary.
controls.description: Evidence: Firewall outbound rule-set; egress filtering policy; approved outbound service list

controls.name: NSCs are installed between all wireless networks and the CDE.
controls.description: Evidence: Network diagram showing wireless/CDE segmentation; wireless NSC config; segmentation test results

controls.name: NSCs are implemented between trusted and untrusted networks.
controls.description: Evidence: Firewall/IPS configuration; trust zone documentation; placement diagrams

controls.name: Inbound traffic from untrusted to trusted networks is restricted to necessary communications only.
controls.description: Evidence: Inbound firewall rules for untrusted-to-trusted flows; approved inbound services list

controls.name: Anti-spoofing measures are implemented to detect and block forged source IP addresses.
controls.description: Evidence: uRPF/ingress ACL configuration; IPS anti-spoofing signatures; test evidence

controls.name: System components storing cardholder data are not directly accessible from untrusted networks.
controls.description: Evidence: Segmentation test results; architecture diagram showing CHD storage system placement

controls.name: Internal IP addresses and routing information are not disclosed to untrusted networks.
controls.description: Evidence: NAT configuration; route summarization policy; BGP/OSPF filtering configs

controls.name: Security controls are implemented on devices that connect to both untrusted networks and the CDE.
controls.description: Evidence: MDM policy; endpoint firewall config; split-tunneling policy; VPN configuration

controls.name: Processes and mechanisms for applying secure configurations to all components are documented, current, and in use.
controls.description: Evidence: Configuration hardening policy; secure baseline standards; version history

controls.name: Roles and responsibilities for activities under Requirement 2 are documented, assigned, and understood.
controls.description: Evidence: RACI or job descriptions; signed acknowledgments

controls.name: Configuration standards are developed, implemented, and kept current for all system components.
controls.description: Evidence: Hardening standards (CIS Benchmarks or equivalent); applicability matrix per OS/platform; version history

controls.name: Vendor default accounts are managed: unused defaults removed or disabled; passwords changed before installation.
controls.description: Evidence: Default account inventory; commissioning checklist; change records confirming default credential changes

controls.name: All non-console administrative access is encrypted using strong cryptography.
controls.description: Evidence: SSH/TLS configuration; disabled Telnet/plain HTTP configs; admin access method documentation

controls.name: Only necessary services, protocols, daemons, and functions are enabled on system components.
controls.description: Evidence: Baseline OS build spec; enabled services list; port scans of in-scope systems

controls.name: If insecure services, protocols, or daemons are present, business justification is documented and additional security features are implemented.
controls.description: Evidence: Insecure service register; business justification records; compensating control documentation

controls.name: System security parameters are configured to prevent misuse.
controls.description: Evidence: System hardening configs; CIS benchmark scan results; SIEM security parameter alerts

controls.name: All non-console administrative access is encrypted using strong cryptography.
controls.description: Evidence: SSH/HTTPS admin access configs; certificate management records

controls.name: For wireless environments connected to or transmitting account data, all wireless vendor defaults are changed at installation.
controls.description: Evidence: Wireless device commissioning checklist; SSID naming; WPA2/3 config; default password change records

controls.name: For wireless environments connected to the CDE, wireless encryption keys are changed on personnel departure and at least every 12 months.
controls.description: Evidence: Key rotation policy; change records for wireless keys; departure checklist including key rotation

controls.name: Processes and mechanisms for protecting stored account data are documented, current, and in use.
controls.description: Evidence: Data protection policy; data retention/disposal policy; version history

controls.name: Roles and responsibilities for activities under Requirement 3 are documented, assigned, and understood.
controls.description: Evidence: RACI; job descriptions; signed acknowledgments

controls.name: Account data storage is minimized via a data retention and disposal policy covering all stored account data.
controls.description: Evidence: Data retention policy; data discovery scan results; disposal records; data minimization guidelines

controls.name: SAD (full track data, CVV2, PIN) is not retained after authorization is complete.
controls.description: Evidence: Data discovery scan results showing no SAD post-auth; application data flow documentation; purge logs

controls.name: SAD stored prior to authorization completion is encrypted using strong cryptography.
controls.description: Evidence: Encryption implementation documentation; key management records; application architecture showing pre-auth SAD handling

controls.name: Full PAN is only displayed to those with a legitimate business need; masking is used otherwise (minimum first 6 / last 4 digits).
controls.description: Evidence: Application screenshots showing PAN masking; display policy; role-based access logs

controls.name: Technical controls prevent copy or relocation of PAN when using remote-access technologies.
controls.description: Evidence: Remote access policy; clipboard restriction config (VDI/DLP); screen capture prevention settings

controls.name: PAN is secured via strong one-way hashes, truncation, index tokens, or strong cryptography wherever it is stored.
controls.description: Evidence: Data protection implementation doc; encryption or tokenization design; key management records

controls.name: Hashes used to render PAN unreadable are keyed cryptographic hashes (HMAC) of the entire PAN.
controls.description: Evidence: Hash implementation documentation; algorithm specification (HMAC-SHA256 or equivalent)

controls.name: If disk-level or partition-level encryption is used to render PAN unreadable, it is only applied to removable electronic media.
controls.description: Evidence: Encryption implementation records; media inventory; OS encryption documentation

controls.name: If disk-level or partition-level encryption is used, logical access must be managed separately from native OS authentication.
controls.description: Evidence: Access control documentation for encrypted media; separate credential management records

controls.name: Procedures and processes for protecting cryptographic keys used to protect stored account data are documented and implemented.
controls.description: Evidence: Key management policy; key custodian assignment records; key ceremony documentation

controls.name: A documented description of the cryptographic architecture is maintained, including all algorithms, protocols, and keys in use.
controls.description: Evidence: Cryptographic inventory / architecture document; algorithm register; key inventory

controls.name: Secret and private keys used to protect stored account data are stored in secure forms at all times.
controls.description: Evidence: Key storage implementation records (HSM, encrypted key store); key wrapping documentation

controls.name: Access to cleartext cryptographic key-encrypting keys is restricted to the fewest custodians necessary.
controls.description: Evidence: Key custodian list; access control records for key-encrypting keys; dual-control evidence

controls.name: Cryptographic keys are stored in the fewest possible locations.
controls.description: Evidence: Key location inventory; key storage policy

controls.name: Key management policies cover generation of strong cryptographic keys.
controls.description: Evidence: Key generation policy; algorithm and key-length specifications (AES-256, RSA-2048+)

controls.name: Key management policies cover secure distribution of cryptographic keys.
controls.description: Evidence: Key distribution procedure; secure channel documentation (key ceremony, HSM transfer)

controls.name: Key management policies cover secure storage of cryptographic keys.
controls.description: Evidence: Key storage policy; HSM or encrypted key store configuration

controls.name: Key management policies cover key changes at the end of each cryptoperiod.
controls.description: Evidence: Cryptoperiod policy; key rotation schedule; rotation completion records

controls.name: Key management policies cover retirement or replacement of keys.
controls.description: Evidence: Key retirement procedure; decommission records; key archival policy

controls.name: Manual clear-text cryptographic key-management operations are managed using split knowledge and dual control.
controls.description: Evidence: Split knowledge and dual control policy; key ceremony records; custodian sign-off logs

controls.name: Unauthorized substitution of cryptographic keys is prevented.
controls.description: Evidence: Key integrity verification procedures; FIM or key attestation records

controls.name: Key custodians formally acknowledge their key-custodian responsibilities.
controls.description: Evidence: Signed key-custodian agreements; training records; acknowledgment logs

controls.name: Processes and mechanisms for protecting account data in transit are documented, current, and in use.
controls.description: Evidence: Encryption in transit policy; TLS standards documentation; version history

controls.name: Roles and responsibilities for activities under Requirement 4 are documented, assigned, and understood.
controls.description: Evidence: RACI or job descriptions; signed acknowledgments

controls.name: Strong cryptography is used to safeguard PAN during transmission over open, public networks.
controls.description: Evidence: TLS configuration extracts (nginx/Apache/load balancer); Qualys SSL Labs or equivalent scan results; cipher suite documentation

controls.name: An inventory of all trusted keys and certificates used to protect PAN in transit is maintained.
controls.description: Evidence: Certificate/key inventory with purpose, issuer, expiry, and renewal schedule

controls.name: Certificates used for PAN transmission are confirmed as valid and not expired.
controls.description: Evidence: Certificate monitoring tool alerts; current certificate status report; renewal records

controls.name: PAN is secured with strong cryptography whenever sent via end-user messaging technologies (email, SMS, chat).
controls.description: Evidence: Email DLP policy; secure messaging platform configs; DLP incident records for unencrypted PAN

controls.name: Processes and mechanisms for protecting all systems against malware are documented, current, and in use.
controls.description: Evidence: Anti-malware policy; endpoint protection standard; version history

controls.name: Roles and responsibilities for activities under Requirement 5 are documented, assigned, and understood.
controls.description: Evidence: RACI or job descriptions; signed acknowledgments

controls.name: An anti-malware solution is deployed on all system components, except those confirmed as low-risk via periodic evaluation.
controls.description: Evidence: AV/EDR deployment report; system inventory with protection status; exception register with risk evaluations

controls.name: Anti-malware solutions detect known types of malware and protect against or address the effects of malware.
controls.description: Evidence: AV/EDR product capabilities documentation; scan logs; quarantine/block records

controls.name: Systems not at risk from malware are evaluated periodically to confirm that the risk assessment remains accurate.
controls.description: Evidence: Low-risk exception records; periodic review schedule; updated risk assessments

controls.name: The frequency of periodic evaluations of systems not at risk from malware is defined in the entity's targeted risk analysis.
controls.description: Evidence: Risk analysis document; defined evaluation frequency; approval records

controls.name: Anti-malware solution(s) are kept current via automatic updates.
controls.description: Evidence: AV/EDR update configuration; update logs showing recent definition/version updates

controls.name: Anti-malware solution(s) perform periodic scans and active/real-time scanning.
controls.description: Evidence: Scheduled scan configuration; scan completion logs; real-time protection status

controls.name: If periodic malware scans are performed, the frequency is defined in the entity's targeted risk analysis.
controls.description: Evidence: Risk analysis with defined scan frequency; scan schedule documentation; approval records

controls.name: Anti-malware mechanisms cannot be disabled or altered by users.
controls.description: Evidence: Endpoint protection tamper-protection configuration; admin-only access controls; policy enforcement logs

controls.name: Anti-malware solution logs are retained and available for review.
controls.description: Evidence: AV/EDR log retention policy; SIEM forwarding configuration; log samples

controls.name: Anti-malware solution(s) cannot be disabled or altered without documented exceptions with management approval.
controls.description: Evidence: Exception records with management approval; temporary disable logs; reactivation evidence

controls.name: Processes and automated mechanisms are in place to detect and protect against phishing attacks.
controls.description: Evidence: Email security gateway config; anti-phishing tool configuration; user awareness training records; phishing simulation results

controls.name: Processes and mechanisms for developing and maintaining secure systems and software are documented, current, and in use.
controls.description: Evidence: SDLC policy; secure coding standards; version history

controls.name: Roles and responsibilities for activities under Requirement 6 are documented, assigned, and understood.
controls.description: Evidence: RACI or job descriptions; signed acknowledgments

controls.name: Bespoke and custom software are developed securely by following secure coding guidelines.
controls.description: Evidence: Secure coding standards document referencing OWASP or equivalent; developer training records; code review policy

controls.name: Software development personnel working on bespoke/custom software are trained in secure coding techniques at least annually.
controls.description: Evidence: Annual training records; training curriculum; completion certificates

controls.name: Bespoke and custom software is reviewed prior to release to identify and remediate potential vulnerabilities.
controls.description: Evidence: Code review records; SAST/DAST scan results; peer review sign-offs; security gates in CI/CD pipeline

controls.name: If manual code reviews are performed, code changes are reviewed by someone other than the originating developer.
controls.description: Evidence: Code review records showing reviewer ≠ author; peer review policy; ticketing system evidence

controls.name: Software engineering techniques or other methods are defined and in use to prevent or mitigate common software vulnerabilities.
controls.description: Evidence: Secure coding checklist; SAST/DAST tool configuration; OWASP Top 10 coverage; vulnerability management records

controls.name: Security vulnerabilities are identified and managed via a process that includes subscribing to reputable security vulnerability information sources.
controls.description: Evidence: Threat intel subscriptions (NVD, CISA KEV, vendor advisories); vulnerability management policy; patch management records

controls.name: An inventory of bespoke and custom software is maintained to facilitate vulnerability and patch management.
controls.description: Evidence: Software inventory with version numbers; SBOM where applicable; update tracking records

controls.name: All system components are protected from known vulnerabilities by installing applicable security patches/updates.
controls.description: Evidence: Patch management policy with SLAs (critical: 1 month per v4.0.1); patch status reports; exception register

controls.name: Public-facing web applications are protected against attacks.
controls.description: Evidence: WAF deployment records; WAF policy; penetration test report covering web apps; DAST scan results

controls.name: An automated technical solution that detects and prevents web-based attacks is deployed for public-facing web applications.
controls.description: Evidence: WAF configuration; rule set; blocking mode configuration; false-positive management records

controls.name: All payment page scripts loaded and executed in the consumer's browser are managed.
controls.description: Evidence: Payment page script inventory; script authorization records; SRI (subresource integrity) hashes; CSP headers; change management records

controls.name: Changes to system components are made according to a defined change-control process.
controls.description: Evidence: Change management policy; change tickets; CAB records; emergency change procedures

controls.name: After a change, all applicable PCI DSS requirements are confirmed to be in place and newly identified vulnerabilities are addressed.
controls.description: Evidence: Post-change verification checklists; re-test records; security sign-off on changes

controls.name: Pre-production environments are separate from production and the separation is enforced with access controls.
controls.description: Evidence: Environment architecture documentation; access control records showing dev/test vs. prod separation

controls.name: Roles and functions are separated between production and development/test environments.
controls.description: Evidence: Role assignment records; access control matrix showing separation of duties

controls.name: Live PANs are not used in pre-production environments except where those environments are within the CDE scope.
controls.description: Evidence: Data masking policy; pre-production data management records; masking tool usage logs

controls.name: Test data and accounts are removed before production systems become active.
controls.description: Evidence: Production launch checklist requiring removal of test accounts/data; production readiness review records

controls.name: Processes and mechanisms for restricting access to system components and cardholder data are documented, current, and in use.
controls.description: Evidence: Access control policy; business-need-to-know policy; version history

controls.name: Roles and responsibilities for activities under Requirement 7 are documented, assigned, and understood.
controls.description: Evidence: RACI or job descriptions; signed acknowledgments

controls.name: An access control model is defined and includes granting access based on least privilege and need-to-know.
controls.description: Evidence: Access control model documentation; role definitions; least privilege policy

controls.name: Access is assigned to users, including privileged users, based on job classification and function.
controls.description: Evidence: RBAC matrix; user account provisioning records; job function documentation

controls.name: Required privileges are approved by authorized personnel.
controls.description: Evidence: Access request tickets with management approval; provisioning workflow records

controls.name: All user accounts and access rights are reviewed at least once every six months.
controls.description: Evidence: Semi-annual user access review records; reviewer sign-offs; remediation records for excess access

controls.name: All application and system accounts and related access privileges are assigned and managed per least privilege.
controls.description: Evidence: Service account inventory; access rights per service account; approval records

controls.name: All application and system accounts and related access rights are reviewed at least once every six months.
controls.description: Evidence: Semi-annual service account review records; sign-offs; remediation records

controls.name: All user access to query repositories of stored cardholder data is restricted to the minimum necessary.
controls.description: Evidence: Database access control records; query access logs; RBAC for database access

controls.name: All access to system components and cardholder data is assigned and managed via an access control system.
controls.description: Evidence: IAM system documentation; access provisioning workflow; access control system configuration

controls.name: The access control system(s) are configured to enforce access control settings after each login request.
controls.description: Evidence: IAM configuration; session control settings; re-authentication settings

controls.name: The access control system(s) are set to 'deny all' by default.
controls.description: Evidence: Default-deny configuration evidence; IAM policy documentation; rule precedence documentation

controls.name: Processes and mechanisms for identifying and authenticating access are documented, current, and in use.
controls.description: Evidence: Identity and access management policy; authentication standards; version history

controls.name: Roles and responsibilities for activities under Requirement 8 are documented, assigned, and understood.
controls.description: Evidence: RACI or job descriptions; signed acknowledgments

controls.name: All users are assigned a unique ID before allowing access to system components or cardholder data.
controls.description: Evidence: User provisioning records; Active Directory/IAM user listing; no-shared-account policy

controls.name: Group, shared, or generic accounts or passwords are only used when necessary and managed per additional controls.
controls.description: Evidence: Shared account policy; shared account inventory; exception register with justification

controls.name: Addition, deletion, and modification of user IDs and authentication factors are managed per formal processes.
controls.description: Evidence: User lifecycle management procedure; provisioning/deprovisioning tickets; JML process documentation

controls.name: Access for terminated users is immediately revoked.
controls.description: Evidence: Termination procedure; HR-IT notification process; deprovisioning records with timestamps

controls.name: Inactive user accounts are removed or disabled within 90 days.
controls.description: Evidence: Automated inactivity reports; 90-day review and disable records; IAM configuration showing 90-day threshold

controls.name: Accounts used by third parties are managed per Requirement 8 controls.
controls.description: Evidence: Third-party account inventory; third-party access policy; just-in-time access records

controls.name: If a user session has been idle for more than 15 minutes, re-authentication is required.
controls.description: Evidence: Session timeout configuration (≤15 minutes); system configuration screenshots

controls.name: All user and admin passwords/passphrases meet a minimum length of at least 12 characters (or 8 if system does not support 12).
controls.description: Evidence: Password policy configuration; AD/IAM password policy settings screenshot

controls.name: User and admin passwords/passphrases are properly secured during transmission and storage.
controls.description: Evidence: Password hashing implementation documentation; TLS for authentication screens; LDAP over TLS config

controls.name: Invalid authentication attempts are limited to no more than 10 tries before locking the account.
controls.description: Evidence: Account lockout policy configuration; AD/IAM lockout threshold setting

controls.name: If passwords are used as authentication factors, they meet minimum complexity requirements.
controls.description: Evidence: Password complexity policy configuration; enforcement evidence across all systems

controls.name: Individuals are not allowed to submit a new password the same as any of their last four passwords.
controls.description: Evidence: Password history enforcement (minimum 4 history); IAM policy configuration

controls.name: If passwords are the only authentication factor for user access, they must be changed at least every 90 days OR the system dynamically assesses account security posture.
controls.description: Evidence: Password expiry policy (≤90 days) OR dynamic assessment configuration; enforcement records

controls.name: MFA is implemented for all non-console access into the CDE for personnel with administrative access.
controls.description: Evidence: MFA configuration for admin access; authentication logs showing MFA enforcement; MFA policy

controls.name: MFA is implemented for all access into the CDE.
controls.description: Evidence: MFA configuration for all CDE access; VPN MFA config; authentication logs

controls.name: MFA is implemented for all remote network access originating from outside the entity's network.
controls.description: Evidence: VPN/remote access MFA configuration; remote access policy; authentication logs

controls.name: MFA systems are implemented securely to prevent MFA bypass.
controls.description: Evidence: MFA system configuration; replay attack prevention; out-of-band channel configuration; no-bypass configuration

controls.name: If accounts used by systems or applications can be used for interactive login, they are managed and protected.
controls.description: Evidence: Service account inventory; interactive login restriction policy; service account access logs

controls.name: Passwords for application and system accounts that can be used for interactive login are not hard-coded in scripts, applications, or configuration files.
controls.description: Evidence: Code review records; secrets scanning tool results; vault/secrets manager configuration

controls.name: Passwords for any application and system accounts are protected against misuse.
controls.description: Evidence: Secrets management policy; vault configuration; rotation schedule for service account credentials

controls.name: Processes and mechanisms for restricting physical access to cardholder data are documented, current, and in use.
controls.description: Evidence: Physical security policy; facility access procedure; version history

controls.name: Roles and responsibilities for activities under Requirement 9 are documented, assigned, and understood.
controls.description: Evidence: RACI or job descriptions; signed acknowledgments

controls.name: Appropriate facility entry controls are in place to limit and monitor physical access to systems in the CDE.
controls.description: Evidence: Access control system logs; badge reader configuration; CCTV records

controls.name: Individual physical access to sensitive areas within the CDE is monitored with video cameras or physical access control mechanisms.
controls.description: Evidence: Camera coverage maps; access control log for sensitive areas; retention settings (minimum 3 months)

controls.name: Physical and/or logical controls restrict use of publicly accessible network jacks.
controls.description: Evidence: Network jack policy; 802.1X or port security configuration; physical port lock/cover evidence

controls.name: Physical access to wireless APs, gateways, handheld devices, networking hardware, and telecom lines in the CDE is restricted.
controls.description: Evidence: Physical security inventory for wireless/networking hardware; access restriction evidence (cages, cabinets)

controls.name: Access to consoles in sensitive areas is restricted via locking when not in use.
controls.description: Evidence: Console lock policy; screen lock configuration; physical observation evidence

controls.name: Procedures are implemented for authorizing and managing physical access of personnel to the CDE.
controls.description: Evidence: Personnel access authorization records; access list; access request/approval workflow

controls.name: Procedures are implemented for managing visitor access to the CDE.
controls.description: Evidence: Visitor policy; visitor log; visitor badge procedure; escort policy

controls.name: Visitor badges or identification are surrendered or deactivated before visitors leave the facility.
controls.description: Evidence: Visitor check-out records; badge return procedure; badge deactivation logs

controls.name: A visitor log is used to maintain a physical audit trail of visitor access.
controls.description: Evidence: Visitor log (physical or electronic); log retention records (minimum 3 months)

controls.name: All media with cardholder data is physically secured.
controls.description: Evidence: Media storage policy; locked storage evidence (cabinet logs); media inventory

controls.name: Offline media backups with cardholder data are stored in a secure location.
controls.description: Evidence: Offline backup storage policy; off-site storage agreement; facility security assessment

controls.name: The security of offline media backup locations is reviewed at least annually.
controls.description: Evidence: Annual security review records for off-site locations; review checklist; sign-offs

controls.name: All media with cardholder data is classified in accordance with the sensitivity of the data.
controls.description: Evidence: Media classification policy; media labeling records; sensitivity classification scheme

controls.name: Media with cardholder data sent outside the facility is secured.
controls.description: Evidence: Media transport policy; tracked courier/secure transport records; chain of custody documentation

controls.name: Management approves all media with cardholder data moved outside the facility.
controls.description: Evidence: Management approval records for media transfers; transport authorization logs

controls.name: Inventory logs of all electronic media with cardholder data are maintained.
controls.description: Evidence: Electronic media inventory log; periodic inventory review records

controls.name: Inventories of electronic media with cardholder data are conducted at least annually.
controls.description: Evidence: Annual media inventory records; date of last inventory; discrepancy resolution records

controls.name: Hard-copy materials with cardholder data are destroyed when no longer needed.
controls.description: Evidence: Hard-copy destruction policy; cross-cut shredder records; secure bin usage; certificate of destruction

controls.name: Electronic media with cardholder data is destroyed when no longer needed.
controls.description: Evidence: Electronic media destruction policy; degaussing/secure wipe records; certificate of destruction

controls.name: POI devices that capture payment card data via direct physical interaction are protected from tampering and unauthorized substitution.
controls.description: Evidence: POI device inventory; device inspection records; anti-tampering policy

controls.name: POI device surfaces are periodically inspected to detect tampering and unauthorized substitution.
controls.description: Evidence: Inspection checklist; periodic inspection records; photo evidence of inspection

controls.name: Personnel are trained to be aware of attempted tampering or substitution of POI devices.
controls.description: Evidence: Training records covering POI tampering awareness; training curriculum with tampering indicators

controls.name: A list of POI devices is maintained, including device make, model, location, and serial or other identifier.
controls.description: Evidence: POI device register with make, model, serial, location; last-update date

controls.name: Processes and mechanisms for logging and monitoring all access to system components are documented, current, and in use.
controls.description: Evidence: Logging and monitoring policy; log management standard; SIEM documentation; version history

controls.name: Roles and responsibilities for activities under Requirement 10 are documented, assigned, and understood.
controls.description: Evidence: RACI or job descriptions; signed acknowledgments

controls.name: Audit logs capture all individual user access to cardholder data.
controls.description: Evidence: SIEM configuration; log samples showing user access to CHD systems; log policy

controls.name: Audit logs capture all actions taken by any individual with root or administrative privileges.
controls.description: Evidence: Log samples showing admin/root actions; SIEM alert configuration for privileged actions

controls.name: Audit logs capture all access to audit trails.
controls.description: Evidence: Log samples showing audit trail access; SIEM configuration for log-read events

controls.name: Audit logs capture all invalid logical access attempts.
controls.description: Evidence: Failed login log samples; SIEM failed authentication events; brute-force detection alerts

controls.name: Audit logs capture all use of and changes to identification and authentication mechanisms.
controls.description: Evidence: Log samples for account creation, deletion, password changes, privilege escalation

controls.name: Audit logs capture all changes to and deletions of audit log records.
controls.description: Evidence: Log samples showing log deletion/modification attempts; SIEM integrity alerts

controls.name: Audit logs capture all initialization, stopping, or pausing of audit logging.
controls.description: Evidence: Log samples for audit log service start/stop events; SIEM configuration

controls.name: Audit logs capture all creation and deletion of system-level objects.
controls.description: Evidence: Log samples for object creation/deletion; SIEM object change events

controls.name: Audit logs capture: user ID, event type, date/time, success/failure, origin, and identity/name of affected data/component.
controls.description: Evidence: Log format documentation; sample log records showing all 6 required fields

controls.name: Read access to audit log files is limited to those with a job-related need.
controls.description: Evidence: Access controls on log files; RBAC for log access; access review records

controls.name: Audit log files are protected from unauthorized modifications by technical controls.
controls.description: Evidence: Log immutability configuration (WORM storage, append-only); FIM on log files; SIEM write protection

controls.name: Audit log files, including those for external-facing technologies, are promptly backed up to a secure central log server or SIEM.
controls.description: Evidence: SIEM ingestion configuration; log forwarding config; backup evidence for log data

controls.name: File integrity monitoring or change detection mechanisms are used on audit logs.
controls.description: Evidence: FIM configuration covering log files; FIM alert records

controls.name: Automated mechanisms are used to perform audit log reviews.
controls.description: Evidence: SIEM alert rules; automated review schedule; SIEM dashboard

controls.name: Automated log review processes cover all defined auditable events.
controls.description: Evidence: SIEM use case list; mapping of use cases to required audit events (per Req 10.2.1)

controls.name: Logs of all other system components are reviewed periodically.
controls.description: Evidence: Log review schedule; review records for non-automated systems; reviewer sign-offs

controls.name: The frequency of periodic log reviews is defined in the entity's targeted risk analysis.
controls.description: Evidence: Targeted risk analysis defining log review frequency; management approval

controls.name: Exceptions and anomalies identified during log review are addressed.
controls.description: Evidence: Incident/exception tracking records; follow-up evidence; escalation records

controls.name: Audit log history is retained for at least 12 months, with at least the most recent three months available for immediate analysis.
controls.description: Evidence: Log retention policy; SIEM or log archive configuration; test retrieval of 3-month and 12-month-old logs

controls.name: System clocks and time are synchronized using accepted time-keeping technology.
controls.description: Evidence: NTP configuration on all in-scope systems; NTP server documentation; time synchronization logs

controls.name: Systems are configured to prevent unauthorized modifications of time.
controls.description: Evidence: NTP ACL configuration; admin-only access to time settings; audit records for time changes

controls.name: Time synchronization settings and data are protected from unauthorized access and tampering.
controls.description: Evidence: NTP authentication configuration; time server access controls; monitoring for time discrepancies

controls.name: Failures of critical security controls (IDS/IPS, FIM, AV, access controls, audit logging, firewalls) are detected, alerted, and addressed promptly.
controls.description: Evidence: SIEM alert rules for critical control failures; incident/alert records for control failures

controls.name: Failures of any critical security control are responded to promptly; root cause is identified, documented, and resolved.
controls.description: Evidence: Incident records with root cause analysis (RCA); RCA documentation; remediation evidence

controls.name: Processes and mechanisms for regularly testing security of systems and networks are documented, current, and in use.
controls.description: Evidence: Security testing policy; penetration testing standard; vulnerability management policy; version history

controls.name: Roles and responsibilities for activities under Requirement 11 are documented, assigned, and understood.
controls.description: Evidence: RACI or job descriptions; signed acknowledgments

controls.name: Authorized and unauthorized wireless access points are managed.
controls.description: Evidence: Wireless scanning tool (WIPS/WIDS) configuration; quarterly wireless scan reports; unauthorized AP detection/response records

controls.name: An inventory of authorized wireless access points is maintained.
controls.description: Evidence: Wireless AP inventory with make, model, location, and MAC address; last-updated date

controls.name: Internal vulnerability scans are performed at least once every three months.
controls.description: Evidence: Quarterly internal scan reports; scan schedule; authenticated (credentialed) scan configuration and evidence

controls.name: Internal vulnerability scans are performed after significant changes.
controls.description: Evidence: Change-triggered scan records; scan reports linked to change tickets

controls.name: Internal vulnerability scans are performed by a qualified internal resource or qualified external third party.
controls.description: Evidence: Scanner qualifications; internal resource training/certification; third-party scanner credentials

controls.name: Internal vulnerability scan findings are remediated and a rescan is performed to confirm resolution.
controls.description: Evidence: Remediation records for high/critical findings; rescan reports confirming resolution; exception register for accepted risks

controls.name: External vulnerability scans are performed at least once every three months by an Approved Scanning Vendor (ASV).
controls.description: Evidence: ASV scan reports (passing status); ASV certification evidence; quarterly scan schedule

controls.name: External vulnerability scan findings are remediated and passing scans are achieved.
controls.description: Evidence: Remediation records; re-scan reports showing passing status; ASV dispute process records if applicable

controls.name: A penetration testing methodology is defined, documented, and implemented.
controls.description: Evidence: Penetration testing methodology document covering network and application layers, exploitation, and reporting requirements

controls.name: Internal penetration testing is performed at least annually and after significant changes.
controls.description: Evidence: Annual internal pen test reports; on-change pen test records; testing scope documentation

controls.name: External penetration testing is performed at least annually and after significant changes.
controls.description: Evidence: Annual external pen test reports; tester qualifications (CREST/OSCP or equivalent); on-change pen test records

controls.name: Exploitable vulnerabilities and security weaknesses found during penetration testing are corrected.
controls.description: Evidence: Remediation records for pen test findings; re-test evidence confirming resolution; risk acceptance for accepted findings with management sign-off

controls.name: If segmentation is used to isolate the CDE, segmentation controls are verified at least every six months and after significant change.
controls.description: Evidence: Bi-annual segmentation test reports; methodology documentation; on-change test records

controls.name: Additional requirement for service providers: Pen testing of segmentation controls is performed at least every six months. (SP)
controls.description: Evidence: Bi-annual segmentation pen test reports; scoping documentation showing all service provider testing boundaries

controls.name: Additional requirement for multi-tenant service providers: Support customers for external penetration testing. (SP)
controls.description: Evidence: Customer pen test support policy; customer access provision records; evidence of customer test facilitation

controls.name: Intrusion-detection and/or intrusion-prevention techniques are used to detect and/or prevent intrusions into the network.
controls.description: Evidence: IDS/IPS deployment evidence; signature update logs; alert records; tuning documentation

controls.name: A change-detection mechanism (FIM) is deployed to alert personnel to unauthorized modification of critical files.
controls.description: Evidence: FIM tool deployment evidence; critical file baseline; FIM alert records; response procedure

controls.name: A change- and tamper-detection mechanism is deployed to alert on unauthorized modifications to HTTP headers and payment page contents.
controls.description: Evidence: Payment page monitoring tool deployment evidence; alert records; scope documentation covering all payment pages

controls.name: An overall information security policy is established, published, maintained, and disseminated to all relevant personnel and applicable vendors.
controls.description: Evidence: Information security policy document; distribution records; vendor/partner acknowledgment records

controls.name: The information security policy is reviewed at least annually and updated when the environment changes.
controls.description: Evidence: Annual review records; version history; change-triggered review records

controls.name: The information security policy clearly defines information security roles and responsibilities for all personnel.
controls.description: Evidence: IS policy sections defining roles; RACI; job descriptions

controls.name: Responsibility for information security is formally assigned to a CISO or another information-security-knowledgeable member of executive management.
controls.description: Evidence: CISO appointment documentation; executive security accountability records; organization chart

controls.name: Acceptable use policies for end-user technologies are documented and implemented.
controls.description: Evidence: Acceptable use policy; signed acknowledgments; technology inventory covered by AUP

controls.name: A targeted risk analysis is performed for each PCI DSS requirement that allows flexibility in activity frequency.
controls.description: Evidence: Targeted risk analysis documents per applicable requirement; management approval records

controls.name: A targeted risk analysis is performed for each PCI DSS requirement specified as needing a customized approach.
controls.description: Evidence: Customized approach risk analyses; control design documentation; independent review evidence

controls.name: All cryptographic cipher suites and protocols in use are documented and reviewed at least annually.
controls.description: Evidence: Cryptographic inventory; annual review records; cipher suite deprecation tracking

controls.name: Hardware and software technologies in use are reviewed at least annually to confirm that they continue to receive security fixes and support.
controls.description: Evidence: Technology lifecycle inventory; annual vendor support status review; EOL/EOS tracking register

controls.name: Additional requirement for service providers: Executive management establishes responsibility for protection of cardholder data and a PCI DSS compliance program. (SP)
controls.description: Evidence: Executive charter for PCI DSS compliance; management acknowledgment; named executive accountability

controls.name: Additional requirement for service providers: Reviews confirming that personnel follow security policies and procedures are performed at least quarterly. (SP)
controls.description: Evidence: Quarterly compliance review records; review scope and methodology; sign-offs

controls.name: An inventory of system components that are in scope for PCI DSS is maintained, including a description of function/use for each.
controls.description: Evidence: CDE scope inventory with component type, function, owner, and location

controls.name: PCI DSS scope is documented and confirmed at least once every 12 months and upon significant changes.
controls.description: Evidence: Annual scope confirmation documentation; significant-change scope review records; QSA confirmation (if applicable)

controls.name: Additional requirement for service providers: PCI DSS scope is confirmed at least every six months and upon significant changes. (SP)
controls.description: Evidence: Bi-annual scope confirmation records; sign-offs; on-change scope review records

controls.name: A formal security awareness program is implemented to make all personnel aware of the information security policy and procedures.
controls.description: Evidence: Security awareness program documentation; training schedule; completion records

controls.name: The security awareness program is reviewed at least annually and updated as needed.
controls.description: Evidence: Annual review records; version history; update log

controls.name: Personnel receive security awareness training upon hire and at least annually.
controls.description: Evidence: New hire training records; annual re-training records; LMS completion reports

controls.name: Security awareness training includes awareness of threats and vulnerabilities that could impact the CDE.
controls.description: Evidence: Training curriculum covering phishing, social engineering, CHD handling, password security, physical security

controls.name: Security awareness training includes awareness about the acceptable use of end-user technologies.
controls.description: Evidence: Training content referencing AUP; AUP acknowledgment post-training

controls.name: Potential personnel who will have access to the CDE are screened prior to hire, within the constraints of local laws.
controls.description: Evidence: Background check policy; background check records for CDE-access personnel; screening scope documentation

controls.name: A list of all third-party service providers (TPSPs) with whom account data is shared or that could affect security of account data is maintained.
controls.description: Evidence: TPSP register with service type, data shared, and contact details

controls.name: Written agreements with all TPSPs acknowledge their responsibility for the security of account data they possess or could affect.
controls.description: Evidence: TPSP agreements with PCI DSS clauses; responsibility acknowledgments

controls.name: An established process for engaging TPSPs includes proper due diligence prior to engagement.
controls.description: Evidence: TPSP onboarding policy; due diligence questionnaire; pre-engagement security assessment records

controls.name: A program to monitor TPSPs' PCI DSS compliance status is implemented at least annually.
controls.description: Evidence: Annual TPSP compliance review records; AOC/SAQ collection; compliance register with expiry dates

controls.name: Information is maintained about which PCI DSS requirements are managed by each TPSP and which are managed by the entity.
controls.description: Evidence: Responsibility matrix per TPSP (shared responsibility matrix); contractual documentation of responsibility split

controls.name: Additional requirement for service providers: TPSPs provide written acknowledgment/assurance to customers about PCI DSS requirements they are responsible for. (SP)
controls.description: Evidence: Responsibility acknowledgment letters; AOC shared with customers; contract clauses detailing SP scope

controls.name: Additional requirement for service providers: TPSPs support customers' requests for information related to their PCI DSS compliance. (SP)
controls.description: Evidence: Customer request handling process; records of customer inquiries and responses

controls.name: An incident response plan exists and is ready to be activated in the event of a system breach.
controls.description: Evidence: Incident response plan (IRP) covering CHD breach scenarios; contact list; escalation procedures; breach notification procedures

controls.name: At least once every 12 months, the incident response plan is reviewed and tested.
controls.description: Evidence: Annual IRP test records (tabletop exercise or live drill); review sign-offs; lessons-learned documentation

controls.name: Specific personnel are designated to be available on a 24/7 basis to respond to suspected or confirmed security incidents.
controls.description: Evidence: 24/7 on-call roster; escalation contact list; documented on-call procedures

controls.name: Personnel responsible for responding to suspected and confirmed security incidents are appropriately and regularly trained.
controls.description: Evidence: IR team training records; tabletop exercise participation records; IR-specific training curriculum

controls.name: The incident response plan includes monitoring and responding to alerts from security monitoring systems.
controls.description: Evidence: IRP sections covering SIEM/IDS/FIM alerts; playbooks for common alert types; escalation procedures

controls.name: The incident response plan is modified and evolved according to lessons learned and industry developments.
controls.description: Evidence: IRP version history; lessons-learned records from incidents and tests; review schedule

controls.name: Incident response procedures are in place for detection of stored PAN where it should not be.
controls.description: Evidence: IRP section covering unauthorized PAN discovery; data classification and remediation procedures
